item.title: 25 Years After 9/11, a Nation Gathers to Remember
item.description: Solemn ceremonies at ground zero in New York, and across the United States, mourned the thousands of lives lost. President Trump paid tribute to the victims in a speech at the Pentagon.
item.dc:creator: The New York Times
item.media:credit: Dave Sanders for The New York Times

item.title: New York Marks the 25th Anniversary of 9/11 at Ground Zero
item.description: At a ceremony in Lower Manhattan, elected officials and loved ones of those killed in the 2001 terror attacks gathered in solemn remembrance.
item.dc:creator: Michael Wilson
item.media:credit: Dave Sanders for The New York Times
item.media:description: At the memorial pools where the World Trade Center towers stood, relatives and visitors can read the etched names of the nearly 3,000 people killed on Sept. 11, 2001.

item.title: A Tale of Two U.S. Opens: $20,000 vs. $100 (Yacht Not Included)

item.title: Facing Islamophobia, Mamdani Keeps Focus on 9/11 Victims
item.description: In recent weeks, Mayor Zohran Mamdani has visited firehouses around New York City as part of an effort to direct the public’s attention toward the victims, and away from himself.

item.media:description: Murad Awawdeh, the president of the New York Immigration Coalition, turned to civil rights work in response to the backlash against Muslims after the Sept. 11 attacks.

item.dc:creator: Maya King
item.media:description: A police officer stood outside the Central Synagogue in Manhattan last year during Yom Kippur, the holiest day on the Jewish calendar.

item.title: She Ran Out of a Tunnel on 9/11. Hours Later, She Gave Birth.

item.title: Legionnaires’ Outbreak in the Bronx Kills One and Infects 4 Others

item.title: Manhattan Bus Lane Plan for 34th Street May Be Stuck in Gridlock
item.description: Months after Mayor Zohran Mamdani said the city would proceed with a redesign of 34th Street that had been halted by the Trump administration, the plan is no closer to completion.
item.dc:creator: Stefanos Chen
item.media:description: The plan would redesign a busy commercial stretch of 34th Street in Manhattan between Third and Ninth Avenues, in the hopes of speeding up bus service.
